solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Obsequious? No city chaps can be so!

indicators.note: saying these letters can be something else invites rearranging them into a new word

blocks.note: all eleven letters of these three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A jibe that City of London financiers are never fawning, said with mock indignation.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'so!' at the end points back to the definition: the scrambled letters can be 'so', that is, obsequious.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant flatters powerful people to win favour, so fawning, servile behaviour is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Concession made by idiot after change of heart

indicators.note: the heart is the middle letter, and changing it swaps it for a different one

blocks.note: a sap is a fool; its middle letter becomes O

explanation.surface: A fool finally gives way after changing their mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A sop is something small offered to placate or appease someone, so it is a token concession.

clue.text: Arrested in putsch, king has cause to breathe with difficulty

indicators.note: someone arrested is held in custody, so the letter is held inside the other word

blocks.note: a putsch is a coup
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch, detained during an uprising, has reason to gasp.
explanation.definitionFit: Croup is a childhood respiratory infection causing a barking cough and laboured, noisy breathing.

clue.text: Polish administrator putting down resistance

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting a letter down shifts it lower in the word, a small rearrangement; resistance is the physics symbol

blocks.note: a prefect is an administrator, as in a French department

explanation.surface: A Polish official suppressing an underground movement.
explanation.walkthrough: R stands for resistance; in PREFECT it moves one place down the column to give the answer. Polish loses its capital: it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To perfect something is to refine it until flawless, which is what polishing a skill or piece of writing does.

clue.text: You might have to pay for this confession

definitions.text: You might have to pay for this

blocks.clueFragment: You might have to pay for this
blocks.note: first meaning: entry to a venue, which often costs money
second meaning: an acknowledgement of guilt

explanation.surface: Suggests that owning up to something will cost you.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the entry fee or right of entry to a place and an acknowledgement that something is true.

clue.text: Little covered in Times post

indicators.note: a thing covered is wrapped round on both sides, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: T for time, doubled for the plural
wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A small item featured in the newspaper's post.
explanation.walkthrough: Times and post suggest the newspaper; post here is a social media message.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweet is a short message published on the social network formerly called Twitter, so it is an online post.

clue.text: Increasingly tawdry stunt involving ambassador

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up or include, so the stunt word encloses the other

blocks.note: a caper is an escapade or prank
HE for His Excellency, an ambassador's title

explanation.surface: A diplomat caught up in an ever more tacky publicity stunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap can mean shoddy or vulgar; the comparative form describes something that has become more vulgar and shoddy.

clue.text: Caligula’s so cruel, almost to the end

indicators.note: going almost to the end means stopping just short, so the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: a sick joke is a cruel one

explanation.surface: A remark on the Roman emperor Caligula's notorious cruelty lasting right to his death.
explanation.walkthrough: Caligula is there to flag Latin: his word for 'so' is the answer, the term editors print to mean 'thus, as written'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Latin the adverb meaning thus or in this manner is sic, which a Roman emperor would have spoken.

clue.text: Delay, putting nothing unusual in stable

indicators.note: putting one thing in another is placing it inside, so the enclosed pair goes within

blocks.note: zero looks like the letter O
something new is novel and out of the ordinary
a stall is a compartment in a stable

explanation.surface: A groom stalls by putting nothing out of the ordinary in the horse box.
explanation.definitionFit: To stonewall is to obstruct or hold things up with evasive tactics, so it means to delay.

clue.text: Being sensible, reached deal after arrangement

definitions.note: a participle phrase for an adjective

indicators.note: arrangement means putting in a new order, so the preceding letters are reordered

blocks.note: the letters to be reworked

explanation.surface: Negotiators sensibly reach a deal after making arrangements.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone clear-headed thinks lucidly and rationally, which is what being sensible and level-headed amounts to.

clue.text: Timetable for Mass

blocks.note: to be pro something is to be for it
a gramme is a unit of mass

explanation.surface: Looks like asking for the schedule of a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Mass with its capital looks religious, but it is the physical quantity measured in grammes.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme of events sets out what happens when, which is what a schedule or timetable does.

clue.text: Run off with reactionary East European

indicators.note: a reactionary wants to go back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: standard compass abbreviation
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: A tale of someone absconding with a right-wing Eastern European.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly, usually with a lover in order to marry, so running off fits.

clue.text: Tree from Mediterranean island, I hear

indicators.note: what the setter hears is a sound, so the spelling of the island name is changed while its pronunciation stays

blocks.note: the eastern Mediterranean island nation

explanation.surface: Suggests a tree species native to an island in the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: The cypress is a tall evergreen conifer, often dark and slender, common in Mediterranean landscapes and graveyards.

clue.text: Constant congestion unsettled the authorities

indicators.note: something unsettled has been disturbed out of place, so the letters move

blocks.note: c is the symbol for the speed of light, a constant
these ten letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Endless traffic jams have rattled the officials in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The authorities sounds like officialdom, but means experts, people who are authorities on a subject.
explanation.definitionFit: The cognoscenti are people with expert knowledge in a field, so they are the recognised authorities on it.

clue.text: Best fashion show on TV?

blocks.note: the top one is the best
gear is clothing, the stuff of fashion

explanation.surface: Asks which is the finest fashion programme on television.
explanation.walkthrough: Top Gear is a long-running BBC motoring programme, nothing to do with clothes, which is the joke of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Top Gear is a popular British television motoring series, so it is a specific instance of a TV show.

clue.text: Soldier beginning to goad weakest in group

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: opening letter of the word
the runt is the weakest of a litter

explanation.surface: A sergeant starts prodding the feeblest recruit in the squad.
explanation.definitionFit: Grunt is American slang for a low-ranking infantry soldier, the ordinary foot soldier doing the heavy work.

clue.text: Drove dangerously, as funeral director did?

blocks.note: first meaning: in British driving slang, passed another car on the inside lane
second meaning: playfully, what an undertaker did, taking on the job of burials

explanation.surface: A hearse driver speeding recklessly.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, to undertake is to pass a slower vehicle on the wrong (inside) side, which is illegal on motorways.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both overtaking on the inside lane and, whimsically, doing what an undertaker does; plainly it also means took on a task.

clue.text: Wearing expensive coat I dined, provoking anger

definitions.note: a participle phrase for a base verb: 'infuriate' means 'provoke anger'

blocks.note: you are in what you wear
a fur is a costly coat
taken as written
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone eats out in a fur coat and annoys animal-rights campaigners.
explanation.definitionFit: To infuriate is to make someone extremely angry, which is to provoke their anger or rage.

clue.text: Kindly butcher providing this for glutton?

blocks.note: surface reading: a generous butcher giving away offal at no charge
setter's reading: the gift, read as one hyphenated word, names a person who indulges heavily in food and drink

explanation.walkthrough: The generous butcher hands over organ meat gratis; read as a compound, those words describe a self-indulgent person.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-liver is someone who indulges freely in eating and drinking, so the term describes a glutton or bon vivant.

clue.text: Order unit to intercept arms

indicators.note: something that intercepts gets in the way, so it is placed in the middle of the other word

blocks.note: ordnance is military weapons and ammunition
I as the Roman numeral one, a unit

explanation.surface: A commander orders a squad to stop a weapons shipment.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an official decree or regulation, especially a municipal law, so it is a kind of order.

clue.text: Possible Belfast firm that is preserving singular cooking method

indicators.note: to preserve something is to keep it safe within, so the letter is held inside

blocks.note: Belfast is in Northern Ireland, NI; 'possible' since Belfast is just one place there
abbreviation for company
i.e., id est, that is
grammatical abbreviation

explanation.surface: A Belfast company keeping alive a unique way of cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: Preserving and cooking method suggest pickling, but the answer is the Nice style of dish, as in salade niçoise.
explanation.definitionFit: À la niçoise describes food prepared in the style of Nice, typically with tomatoes, olives, garlic and anchovies.

clue.text: Road round Corsica perhaps making one annoyed

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation
Corsica is French, so it is an île, French for island; 'perhaps' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A frustrating drive on the winding coast road around Corsica.
explanation.definitionFit: Riled is an informal word for irritated or angered, so it describes someone who has been annoyed.

clue.text: University, particular one associated with Republican defeat

blocks.note: Rep. is the US abbreviation for Republican
standard abbreviation
a particular university, the London School of Economics

explanation.surface: A college and one of its departments are linked with a Republican electoral loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'particular one' means a particular university, following on from University; Republican comes first in the answer though last in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To repulse an attack is to drive it back, so it means to defeat or repel an enemy.

clue.text: About to join expert in boat

blocks.note: C for circa, Latin for about
an oracle is an authority people consult

explanation.surface: Someone is about to team up with a specialist aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as one phrase meaning 'on the point of'; split it, and About gives the letter while 'to join' just glues the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A coracle is a small round traditional Welsh and Irish craft made of wicker covered with hide.

clue.text: Relaxed, being pressed to dismiss His Majesty

indicators.note: dismissing someone sends them away, so those letters are taken out

blocks.note: pressed fabric has creases put in
Carolus Rex, King Charles's cipher; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A courtier unwinds after being pushed to sack the King.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased means loosened or made less tense, so it is a synonym for relaxed, as in an eased grip.

clue.text: Boy’s inspired idea — to visit Santa here?

definitions.note: a cryptic pointer to a place rather than a plain noun

indicators.note: to be inspired is literally to have something breathed in, so the second word goes inside the first

blocks.note: a lad is a boy
a plan is an idea for doing something

explanation.surface: A child has a bright idea about a trip to see Father Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular tradition places Father Christmas's home in this northern Finnish region, where families travel to meet him.

clue.text: Get on with some scallywag, re-employed

indicators.note: some of the following words means only part of their run of letters is used

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Getting along with a rascal who has been taken back on.
explanation.definitionFit: People who get on are in harmony; to agree likewise means to be of one mind and live amicably together.

clue.text: Biblical mother-in-law I complain about

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
to moan is to complain

explanation.surface: The age-old joke of grumbling about one's mother-in-law, given a scriptural setting.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Ruth, Naomi is Ruth's mother-in-law, whom Ruth loyally follows back to Bethlehem.

clue.text: Way in which great strides are made?

definitions.text: Way in which great strides are made?

blocks.clueFragment: Way in which great strides are made?
blocks.note: surface reading: a method by which big progress is achieved

blocks.clueFragment: Way in which great strides are made?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a road where fine trousers are made, strides being British slang for trousers

explanation.walkthrough: Strides is British slang for trousers, and 'way' is a street; making great strides normally means progressing well.
explanation.definitionFit: This London street in Mayfair is famous for its bespoke tailors, who make high-quality suits and trousers.

clue.text: Feeble cook keeling over, losing face

indicators.note: the face is the front, so the first letter is lost
a boat keeling over turns upside down, so in a down entry the letters run the other way

blocks.note: to stew is to cook slowly

explanation.surface: A weak chef collapses and is humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: Wet is British slang for a feeble, ineffectual person.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage wet describes someone weak, spineless or lacking resolve, the sense of feeble.

clue.text: Type to cheat, billions going missing

indicators.note: something that goes missing is no longer there, so it is taken out of the word

blocks.note: to bilk is to swindle
B is the abbreviation for billion(s); this letter is removed

explanation.surface: A kind of fraudster who swindles while billions vanish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilk means a sort or kind, as in 'people of that ilk', so it matches type in the sense of category.

clue.text: Support scruffy modern teens

indicators.note: scruffy means messy and untidy, so the letters are in disorder

blocks.note: the letters to be reworked

explanation.surface: Backing for untidy present-day adolescents.
explanation.definitionFit: An endorsement is a public statement of approval or backing for a person, product or cause.
